data.narrative:
Clone Robotics is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Dhanush Radhakrishnan and Lucas Kozlik that has raised $7.1M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 11 private peers in Robotics & Manufacturing, supplemented by 1 public comparable (277810.KQ). Notable private peers include Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI, though the fragmented nature of this sector limited direct peer matching.

Only one valuation method proved applicable: Stage-Progression analysis. Using the $7.1M raised as a proxy for post-money value, applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier—standard for Seed to next-stage advancement—yields an implied valuation of $17.75M. Peer-median comparison was not applicable; while 11 same-sector companies exist, fewer than three satisfied narrow filters for stage, adjacency, or valuation tier, making a subset-based median unreliable. A full-sector median would introduce material estimation risk given robotics subsector heterogeneity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $20.4M, with a median point of $18M. This range reflects the stage-progression anchor ±15% to account for early-stage variance. Key uncertainties include the lack of tight peer comparables at identical stage and tier, the undisclosed nature of prior round terms, and the absence of revenue or traction data. Additional fundraising data and operational metrics would strengthen conviction in this range.
